transcript:
Header:
Date: 2026-03-20
Time: 15:00 - 15:48 UTC
Duration: 48 minutes
Attendees: Sophie Chen (Redwood AE), Raj Patel (Redwood SE), Lena Ortiz (Redwood CSM), Karen Morales (Elmbridge CISO), Alan Ng (Head of Infra), Priya Singh (Compliance), Tom Brewer (SRE)

Summary: (auto) Quick run through of incident response and BCDR specifics; customer looking for clear RTO/RPO numbers and contractual SLA wording plus how escalation works into Redwood support / engineering.

-- Transcript --
[00:00] Sophie (Redwood AE): Hey everyone, thanks for joining, i'm Sophie with Redwood, joining me is Raj, our solutions engineer. Quick roll call?
[00:06] Karen (Elmbridge CISO): Karen here.
[00:07] Alan: Alan here.
[00:09] Priya: Priya on compliance.
[00:11] Tom: Tom, SRE.
[00:13] Raj (Redwood SE): great to meet you all. We'll focus on incident response and BCDR today, happy to dive into runbooks.
[00:20] Sophie: quick agenda: SOC 2 & ISO artifacts, encryption/KMS, audit logs, then incident response & BCDR (RTO/RPO), SLA uptime and escalation process. sound good?
[00:27] Karen: yes, especially interested in RTO/RPO and escalation into on-call engineering. we've seen gaps in other vendors.
[00:35] Raj: understood. to set context, Redwood's hosted offering has a control plane we manage and an option for private deployments. for hosted we have multi-region failover and automated backups, and for dedicated/private we can do region pinning and customer KMS.
[00:47] Tom: can you clarify backups? how frequent, and what's the restore time?
[00:50] Raj: for the hosted API our standard snapshot cadence is every 4 hours, with transaction logs retained for 30 days. typical recovery for metadata/config is under 1 hour for partial recovery; for a full cluster restore from snapshot into a cold cluster our standard RTO is targeted at 8 hours, RPO ~4 hours.
[01:10] Alan: 8 hours full restore is a bit high for us; for critical production traffic we need RTO under 2 hours.
[01:15] Sophie: understood, that maps to dedicated/reserved capacity customers— we can offer reduced RTO with Dedicated and private deployments, and we have options for hot-standby and cross-region active-passive failover. for a dedicated plan with hot-standby we can hit RTO ~30-60 minutes and RPO near zero for session state via synchronous replication.
[01:33] Priya: synchronous replication implies latency impact and cost trade-offs, correct?
[01:37] Raj: yes, synchronous replication increases cost and can affect tail latency; we typically recommend it for tier-1 workloads. for many customers, an active-passive with nearline replication (async) balances cost and RTO.
[01:48] Karen: on the contractual SLA— what's your uptime guarantee and how are credits calculated?
[01:52] Sophie: our standard hosted SLA is 99.9% monthly availability. Dedicated customers can get 99.95% with specific commit. credits scale: under 99.9% we offer pro-rated credits; for enterprise addendum we can negotiate higher SLOs + penalties. we'll share the exact SLA table after the call.
[02:06] Tom: how do you measure availability? do you count scheduled maintenance?
[02:09] Raj: we measure availability at the model endpoint level, excluding scheduled maintenance windows where customers are notified 48 hours in advance unless emergency maintenance is required; emergency maintenance is rare and we provide post-incident reports.
[02:20] Alan: escalation — if we hit a production outage, what does your on-call look like?
[02:24] Raj: our support tiers: standard support goes to support engineers; enterprise + dedicated has 24/7 on-call with an engineering escalation path. escalation matrix is: customer raises with support -> triage -> on-call infra team -> SE/engineering engagement -> exec on-call for major incidents. we integrate with PagerDuty and can accept direct SAML/SSO authenticated cases.
[02:43] Karen: do you have a defined SLA for time-to-engage (first response) on Sev1?
[02:48] Sophie: for enterprise we commit to 15 minute initial response on Sev1, 1 hour for Sev2. For hosted self-serve it's longer (within 1 business hour). We'll put these in the SLA addendum.
[02:58] Priya: audit logs: retention, format, tamper proofing?
[03:02] Raj: audit logs are stored in an append-only store, retention configurable up to 7 years; default is 90 days for hosted. logs include API access, key rotations, admin actions. For private deployments you can route logs to your SIEM (we support syslog, Splunk, S3 export).
[03:20] Priya: KMS — key management: do you manage keys or integrate with customer KMS?
[03:26] Raj: we offer both. hosted customers can use Redwood-managed keys; enterprise/dedicated/private can integrate with customer KMS (AWS KMS, GCP KMS, Azure Key Vault or bring-your-own HSM). we support envelope encryption and separated key material for customer data.
[03:38] Alan: how are keys rotated and what's the impact on live sessions?
[03:41] Raj: rotation is configurable; we support online key rotation with zero-downtime for data encrypted via envelope keys; for some legacy flows a re-encryption job runs in background. we'll share the key-rotation procedure doc.
[03:52] Karen: incident response — do you have a runbook for notifying customers and for remediation steps?
[03:56] Raj: yes. high-level flow: detect -> classify -> contain -> eradicate -> recover -> post-incident review. notifications: initial notification within 30 minutes of detection for Sev1 with interim updates every hour until resolved, final RCA within 5 business days.
[04:10] Tom: interim updates every hour is fine. what about data exfiltration scenarios?
[04:14] Raj: for confirmed data exfiltration we invoke additional protocols: legal/forensics engagement, long-term retention holds, and we follow customer contractual notification requirements including regulators. we can support joint communication templates.
[04:26] Priya: do you provide SOC2 Type II and ISO 27001?
[04:29] Sophie: yes, we are SOC 2 Type II and ISO 27001 certified; i'll share the report and cert link after. note: the SOC 2 report will have redactions for vendor-sensitive details, but it covers the controls for security and availability.
[04:40] Karen: can we get a detailed list of sub-service providers and a third-party risk matrix?
[04:44] Sophie: yes, we'll include our subprocessor list and their assurance summaries.
[04:48] Alan: technical question — for the failover test, how do you simulate region outage and what's the expected disruption?
[04:54] Raj: for hosted active-passive we can fail traffic to standby region; typical failover causes brief connection resets and reconnects at client side, token generation may have short latency spike for first requests as caches warm. we recommend performing staged failover during low traffic windows; for Dedicated we can configure cross-region active-active to reduce impact.
[05:12] Tom: do you have DR runbook examples you can share?
[05:15] Raj: yes, i will attach a sample runbook with checklist, playbooks, and command snippets.
[05:20] Priya: regarding contractual SLA credits, are they capped?
[05:23] Sophie: yes credits are capped as a percentage of monthly fees—standard tier is capped at 50% of monthly bill for repeated outages; for enterprise we can negotiate.
[05:30] Karen: escalation path into engineering — if support can't triage, how fast does an engineer join?
[05:34] Raj: enterprise: engineer on-call joins within 30 minutes for Sev1 after escalation; further escalation to product/infra leads within 2 hours, exec notification per incident severity.
[05:44] Alan: we need the exact names and contact methods for your on-call, and confirmation of PagerDuty integration for our runbooks.
[05:50] Sophie: we'll provide the on-call matrix and confirm PD integration; PD service hooks can be set to push alerts into your ops channels, and we support SAML-based SSO for console access.
[06:00] Tom: testing — we'd like to run a live failover test with Redwood in a staging window. what's the process?
[06:04] Raj: we can do a planned failover test: coordinate maintenance window, Redwood performs failover in test env, both teams monitor, and we run rollback steps if issues. we'll provide a test plan and acceptance criteria.
[06:15] Karen: regulatory — data residency: can you guarantee EU-only or US-only data at rest?
[06:19] Sophie: yes, with Private deployments or Dedicated region-pinning we can guarantee data residency. hosted tenants can be region-restricted with contractual commitments for data-at-rest location.
[06:29] Priya: logging retention for audit: we need 7 years for certain records. is that supported?
[06:33] Raj: yes configurable up to 7 years for audit logs in our enterprise offering; we can export to Elmbridge's S3 bucket for long-term retention.
[06:42] Alan: encryption in transit and at rest? TLS 1.2/1.3 in transit; at rest AES-256 with customer KMS if required.
[06:50] Sophie: correct.
[06:52] Karen: about post-incident RCA — is that scoped and is there a template we can expect?
[06:57] Raj: we produce a post-incident report with timeline, root cause, mitigation, and preventative measures; we also include playbook changes. delivery target is 5 business days, expedited upon request.
[07:08] Tom: curious about monitoring and alerting — do you provide SLO dashboards and per-endpoint metrics?
[07:12] Raj: yes, Redwood Console exposes per-endpoint latency, error rates, token consumption and SLO dashboards; we also provide tracing hooks for sampling.
[07:22] Priya: any surprises or edge cases we should be aware of?
[07:25] Raj: one nuance: if customers use third-party models hosted elsewhere via our routing, the model provider's limits can affect RTO— we recommend pinning model versions inside Redwood for critical paths.
[07:36] Karen: ok last part — contract language. we need SLA annex that specifies RTO/RPO for Dedicated, escalation contacts, credits, data residency and data breach notification timelines.
[07:46] Sophie: noted. we'll produce an SLA annex draft that includes all those items and circulate.
[07:51] Lena (CSM): i'll coordinate scheduling the SRE technical run-through and the failover test window.
[07:57] Sophie: great. quick recap of next steps...
[07:59] Raj: i'll send the runbook, key rotation doc, and sample playbook.
[08:03] Sophie: i'll send SOC2/ISO artifacts, subprocessors, and draft SLA annex.
[08:07] Priya: we'll share Elmbridge's RTO/RPO requirements and proposed test dates.
[08:12] Karen: thanks everyone, looking forward to the docs.
[08:15] Sophie: thanks all, we'll follow up this week.
